questions.q: What does Gerber call the belief that technical skill equals business skill?
questions.why: From the lesson on technical skills, Gerber names the entrepreneurial myth as the false belief that technical expertise equals business ability.

questions.q: According to the book, what proportion of small businesses never pass the 5-year mark?
questions.why: From the lesson on technical skills, the book states 4 out of 5 small businesses never make it past the 5-year mark.

questions.q: What does Gerber suggest you imagine when planning your business from day one?
a: That you are building your first franchise store
That you are hiring a professional manager
That you are opening a second location
That you are competing against a national chain
questions.why: From the lesson on thinking like a franchise, Gerber advises imagining you are building your first franchise store to drive systematization.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a hard system in Gerber's framework?
questions.why: From the lesson on system of systems, hard systems are defined as inanimate objects, with a coffee machine given as the example.

questions.q: What is the core principle behind building a system of systems?
a: Your business should not depend on individual people's skills
Your business should rely on one key employee
Your business should avoid all documentation
Your business should grow by adding more locations
questions.why: From the lesson on system of systems, the goal is a business that does not rely on people's skills but on interconnected systems.
